id_face_canyon.blurb: Face Canyon is a basalt wall in the Black Cliffs, the columnar cliff band along Highway 21 east of Boise, tucked between Car Body and Scary canyons. It sits in a shallow recess in the cliff line, and its lines feel longer than most at this crag. Twenty-three routes split almost evenly between crack and gear climbs and bolted sport lines, with grades running from 5.8 up to 5.11 and the bulk sitting between 5.9 and 5.11. It suits climbers who already lead moderate to hard grades and want both rack and quickdraw options on one wall. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons here, since summer afternoons get very hot.

id_tall_cliffs.blurb: The Tall Cliffs are the section of the Black Cliffs, along Highway 21 east of Boise, where the basalt stands a bit higher than usual. The wall catches sun for much of the day. Twenty-two routes mix sport lines with traditional leads and a few top-rope setups. Almost everything is 5.9 and harder: a handful of 5.9s, a large block of 5.10s, and a good number of 5.11s, so it is a better fit for intermediate and stronger climbers than for beginners. A trail leads up to the base from the large gravel lot. As elsewhere at this crag, spring and fall are the pleasant seasons and summer is hot.

id_lower_fifth_canyon.blurb: Lower Fifth Canyon is a quiet side canyon in Q'emiln Park near Post Falls, North Idaho, on the Spokane River. The rock is gneiss, climbed on vertical to slightly steep faces. Most of the twenty-two routes are bolted sport lines, with a few gear routes and a single top-rope. Grades run from the high 5.7s through 5.12, with the heaviest concentration in 5.10 and 5.11, plus a small group of easier climbs for warming up. Walls mostly face south and southeast to southwest, so they pick up sun through much of the day. The canyon sees little traffic, though the walk down into it takes some effort.

id_stairs_left_north.blurb: Stairs Left/North is one of the boulder groups at Dierkes Lake near Twin Falls, on the lake's north shore in the Snake River Canyon. The problems lie to the left of a conspicuous flight of steps running through the line of boulders. Basalt here is heavily featured, with pockets, monos, underclings and a slab arete, so the climbing leans on finger strength and body tension. Twenty-two problems range from easy V0 and V1 warm-ups, which make up most of the list, to a few at V3 and V4 and one V5. A short walk across the bridge from the parking area gets you there, and the lake area is known as a mild winter option.

id_martini_sector.blurb: Martini Sector is the lowest part of the Discovery Wall, a tall, impressive wall at the Fins in central Idaho at high elevation. It is a pure sport venue with twenty-two bolted routes, all in the 5.11 range or harder: a few at 5.11, a strong group in the 5.12s, and a serious tail of 5.13 and 5.14 climbs, including what is described as the hardest sport route in the state. This is a destination for strong sport climbers rather than anyone building up to the grade. Reaching the wall takes a downhill hike of roughly a quarter hour from the parking area.
